The scene is one unit of a street parade filmed from a fixed elevated position looking up the street (the same shop signs, parked cars and centre line are visible throughout, so the motion is real and not a camera-pan illusion).

At about 516–520 seconds a girl leads a small pony in the foreground, nearest the camera. The pony wears a light blanket with a two-line message reading roughly "WALK SAFETY". Directly behind her, up the street, rides a group of children and teenagers on bicycles, including two caped/poncho riders with helmets, one of them carrying a rectangular sign mounted across the handlebars. Frame-to-frame displacement against the static parked cars and road markings shows the girl, the pony and all of these bicycles moving the same way: toward the camera, i.e. down-street with the parade.

At about 522–533 seconds the camera zooms out to a wide view. The same bicycle group is now in the centre of the street, still moving toward the camera, with a column of marching soldiers and then trucks following behind them up the street. On the far left of the frame, hugging the left curb where no parade formation is marching, a single cyclist moves steadily away from the camera, i.e. up-street. Tracked across consecutive frames he enters from the foreground, rides straight up the empty left edge past the bicycles, then past the soldiers, and keeps going into the far background until he disappears among the distant crowds and floats. He never veers into the formation, never slows to the parade's pace, and never rides with the group.

He therefore travels in the opposite direction because he is not part of that bicycle unit and is not following it. He is an independent through-rider using the one strip of roadway the parade leaves free — the clear lane along the far left curb — to travel back up the street against the parade flow, getting past the parade to his own destination. The direction differs because the journeys differ: the unit rides down-street with the parade, while he rides up-street around it on the empty edge.
